title: Unless & Provided That: Setting Exact Conditions

sections.content: You know *siempre que*, *con tal de que* ('provided that / as long as') and *a menos que* ('unless') with the subjunctive from B1 Unit 21, *salvo que* from B2 Unit 9, *siempre y cuando* from B2 Unit 11 and *en caso de que* from C1 Unit 6. In contracts, deadlines and negotiations, the skill is choosing the right conjunction for the logic of the agreement: *a menos que* (and formal *salvo que*) states the **only exception** that blocks a result (*No pospondremos la entrega a menos que haya una urgencia*), while *con tal de que* and *siempre que* (or *siempre y cuando*) state the **minimum condition** required for something to go ahead (*Acepto el compromiso siempre que nos den margen suficiente*). Every one of these conditional conjunctions requires the **subjunctive**.

sections.title: Conditional conjunctions + subjunctive
rows: States the sole exception ('unless'): *Salimos a las cinco a menos que surja un imprevisto.*
States a minimum requirement ('as long as'): *Adelanto el anexo con tal de que revises los datos.*
Sets a binding condition ('provided that'): *Firmamos el compromiso siempre que se cumpla la condición.*
Prepares for a possible contingency ('in case'): *Llama en caso de que necesites más margen.*

items.spanish: No podemos posponer la entrega a menos que el cliente acepte una prórroga.
items.english: We cannot postpone the delivery unless the client accepts an extension.

items.spanish: Acepto adelantar el trabajo con tal de que me envíes el anexo hoy mismo.
items.english: I agree to bring the work forward as long as you send me the attachment today.

items.spanish: Cumpliremos el compromiso siempre que mantengamos un margen de dos horas.
items.english: We will fulfil the commitment provided that we keep a two-hour leeway.

items.spanish: En caso de que falte alguna condición en el anexo, avísame de inmediato.
items.english: In case any condition is missing from the attachment, let me know right away.

sections.content: Watch the meaning contrast: *a menos que* = 'unless' (negative exception), whereas *con tal de que* / *siempre que* = 'provided that' (positive requirement). In these senses both take the **subjunctive** — never the indicative (*siempre que* + indicative would mean 'whenever').
